cohort: The cohort consisted of 508 infants born weighing 1,000 to 2,499 g admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit, excluding those with feto-maternal transfusion syndrome or hemolytic diseases.
finding: Significant relationships were observed between Early-onset hyperbilirubinemia (EOH) and birth weight, albumin, albumin/globulin ratio, total serum bilirubin, and antenatal corticoid therapy, suggesting that the albumin/globulin ratio may be a useful indicator for EOH among infants weighing 1,000 to 2,499 g.
gest_age: N/A (gestational age was a measured variable, but no specific range for the cohort was provided; the cohort comprised premature infants based on birth weight criteria)
